c1-vitakultura-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Reform Era Views
c1-vitakultura-01.scenario: At a history club evening on the Reform Era, someone asks how Széchenyi and Kossuth differed.
c1-vitakultura-01.prompt: Tell the club how Széchenyi and Kossuth differed in the Reform Era.
c1-vitakultura-01.target: Széchenyi először a gazdasági megerősödést akarta, Kossuth viszont a politikai szabadságot hangsúlyozta.
c1-vitakultura-01.english: Széchenyi wanted economic strengthening first, but Kossuth stressed political freedom.
c1-vitakultura-01.canDo: I can explain the Reform Era debate between Széchenyi and Kossuth.

c1-vitakultura-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Law Without Weapons
c1-vitakultura-02.scenario: At a history club evening, someone asks how Deák Ferenc resisted without weapons.
c1-vitakultura-02.prompt: Tell the club what Deák Ferenc relied on after 1849.
cues: Say what he did not accept
Say what principle he relied on
c1-vitakultura-02.target: Deák nem fogadott el hivatalt, és a jogfolytonosság elvére támaszkodott.
c1-vitakultura-02.english: Deák did not accept office, and he relied on the principle of legal continuity.
c1-vitakultura-02.canDo: I can explain how Ferenc Deák argued from legal continuity (*jogfolytonosság*).

c1-vitakultura-03.title: Communicative Challenge: A Point of Order
c1-vitakultura-03.scenario: At a history club evening, the talk turns to the parliamentary debates of the Dualist period.
c1-vitakultura-03.prompt: Tell the club what obstruction was in the Dualist Parliament.
cues: Say what it wanted to prevent
c1-vitakultura-03.target: Az obstrukció azt jelentette, hogy az ellenzék hosszú beszédekkel akadályozta a szavazást.
c1-vitakultura-03.english: Obstruction meant that the opposition blocked a vote with long speeches.
c1-vitakultura-03.canDo: I can explain what parliamentary obstruction (*obstrukció*) was in Dualist Hungary.

c1-vitakultura-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Pamphlet
c1-vitakultura-04.scenario: At a history club evening, someone asks why pamphlets mattered in Hungarian public life.
c1-vitakultura-04.prompt: Tell the club why pamphlets and newspaper polemics mattered.
c1-vitakultura-04.target: A röpirat gyorsan terjedt, és hatással lehetett a közvéleményre.
c1-vitakultura-04.english: A pamphlet spread quickly and could influence public opinion.
c1-vitakultura-04.canDo: I can explain the role of pamphlets (*röpirat*) and newspaper polemics in Hungarian public debate.

c1-vitakultura-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Debate Online
c1-vitakultura-05.scenario: At a history club evening, the talk turns to debate on social media today.
c1-vitakultura-05.prompt: Tell the club what many people criticise about debate online.
cues: Say what a good debate needs
c1-vitakultura-05.target: Sokak szerint az algoritmusok véleménybuborékokat erősítenek, a jó vitához viszont érvek és meghallgatás kellenek.
c1-vitakultura-05.english: Many say that algorithms strengthen echo chambers, while a good debate needs arguments and listening.
c1-vitakultura-05.canDo: I can explain how critics say algorithms and social media change public debate.

c1-vitakultura-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Three Styles
c1-vitakultura-consolidation.scenario: At the end of the history club evening, you compare three speakers you have read about.
c1-vitakultura-consolidation.prompt: Compare in a sentence or two how two of them argued.
c1-vitakultura-consolidation.target: Széchenyi a lassú reformokban hitt, Deák pedig a jogfolytonosságra épített.
c1-vitakultura-consolidation.english: Széchenyi believed in slow reforms, while Deák built on legal continuity.
c1-vitakultura-consolidation.canDo: I can compare how Széchenyi, Kossuth and Deák argued.
